sections.html:
Hallandale Beach is a small, oddly shaped city on the southern edge of Broward County. The outline dates to a 1947 deal that let it annex land from Federal Highway east to the ocean, while the oceanfront north of Beach Boulevard went to Hollywood. Total area is 4.55 square miles, of which 4.21 is land.

The 2020 census counted 41,217 people and 17,573 households. With that many homes on so little land, check with the city on which zoning and redevelopment rules touch your own parcel before you promise a buyer anything about future use.

sections.h2: How permits work in Hallandale Beach
sections.html:
The Building Division runs two online systems. ePermitsOneStop is a joint city and Broward County site where applicants submit plans so City and County staff review them at the same time. HB Self-Service lets you pay fees, check a permit and schedule inspections. Search by address or parcel and you can see permit history without an account.

That history search is handy before you list. Look up your own address, spot any permit that never reached a final inspection, and ask the Building Division how to close it. Roof, window, electrical and balcony enclosure work are the jobs most likely to surface at a buyer's inspection. The 1926 hurricane and Hurricane Katrina in August 2005 both struck this city, so inspectors often ask about roofs, windows and past insurance claims on older homes. Pull your claim paperwork along with the permits.

Broward County Records, Taxes and Treasury collects the bill and also supports the Value Adjustment Board, which hears disputes over exemptions, classifications and values. The Recording Office is at 115 S. Andrews Ave, Room 114, Fort Lauderdale. Call 954-831-4000 or 3-1-1; the office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The Value Adjustment Board has its own address at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale.

Florida property tax calendar as it applies in Broward
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value is set
March 1Exemption applications due
AugustProposed tax notice mailed; a challenge goes to the clerk within 25 days
November to FebruaryBills arrive; early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent to 1 percent
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent
By June 1Tax certificates sold

• Homestead: the first $25,000 applies to all taxes, and a second layer up to $25,000 applies to assessed value above $50,000 for non-school taxes.
  • Save Our Homes: yearly assessed increases are held to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, and the reset on sale is automatic.
  • Rental: homestead ends once the unit is rented out or stops being your permanent home.
  • Portability: the benefit can follow you to a new Florida homestead if you set it up within three years.

A sale ends the seller's cap. Ask the Broward Property Appraiser how the parcel will be reassessed for the buyer, and expect the new owner's bill to run higher than yours. A buyer's own estimate can differ sharply from what you pay now, so share the tax history early.

sections.h2: Is your house inside the redevelopment area?
sections.html:
The Hallandale Beach Community Redevelopment Agency was created by Ordinance No. 96-25 on December 27, 1996. Its area runs from Pembroke Road on the north to the Dade-Broward County line on the south, and from Interstate 95 on the west to NE 14th Avenue and its canal on the east.

If your house sits inside that boundary, ask the city whether a redevelopment plan changes what a buyer can build. Plans and master plans can shape park access, traffic and the streets around a listing, so a short call to planning staff can answer a buyer's questions before they come up.

Broward uses the standard doc stamp rate: 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, paid to the clerk when the deed is recorded. The higher Miami-Dade rate and its surtax do not apply here. The seller and the buyer are both liable, even when the contract assigns the cost to one side.

Recording is charged per page under section 28.24. A condominium or homeowners association will need to supply an estoppel or payoff letter, and those can add days to a closing, so request it as soon as you have a buyer.

sections.h2: What if the house is occupied, inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
A tenant changes the timeline. Month-to-month tenancies end on 30 days' notice, and a landlord can serve a 3-day notice for unpaid rent. After the landlord wins a judgment, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice before putting the landlord in possession.

If the owner has died, a small estate can sometimes use summary administration, which is open when the non-exempt estate is no more than $150,000 or the decedent has been dead over two years. Foreclosure sales follow 20 to 35 days after judgment. A closing agent or a Florida attorney can tell you which of these applies to you.

Begin with records. Print your permit history, ask the Broward tax collector for the current bill, and request association paperwork if the home is a condo or sits in an HOA. Next, compare ways to sell: an agent listing brings the most showings, a cash buyer can skip lender conditions, and a private sale puts the paperwork on you.

Whichever route you pick, ask for written terms and the date funds reach you. Your closing agent prepares the deed, collects the stamp tax and files it with the clerk, and splits the year's property tax between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Which county is Hallandale Beach in?
faqs.a: Broward County. The area belonged to Dade County until Broward was formed in 1915.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax in Broward County?
faqs.a: Yes, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, collected by the clerk at recording. The Miami-Dade rate does not apply in Broward.

faqs.q: How do I check my permit history?
faqs.a: Use the HB Self-Service portal and search by address, parcel number or inspection number. No account is needed to view finalized documents.

faqs.q: Where do I file a property value challenge?
faqs.a: Petitions go to the clerk within 25 days of the proposed tax notice, and the Broward Value Adjustment Board hears them. Call 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444 with questions.

faqs.q: How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get?
faqs.a: 30 days. For unpaid rent, a landlord first serves a 3-day notice.
